jobs.title: Business Analyst Manager
jobs.desc:
About Citco
JOB DESCRIPTION
Citco is a global leader in fund services, coporate governance and related asset services with staff across 80 offices worldwide. With more than €1 trillion in assets under administration, we deliver end-to-end solutions and exceptional services to meet our clients’ needs.
For more information about Citco, please visit www.citco.com
About The Role
This is a Business Analyst Manager role supporting and working closely with Citco’s Client Lifecycle Management (CLM) team. The CLM team is responsible for Customer Due Diligence (CDD), completing Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) on behalf of the Citco Group Companies. The CLM team plays an important role in ensuring Citco’s regulatory obligations are met and delivering a positive customer experience during the process.
To support the continued development of the CLM function, Citco is looking to recruit a Business Analyst Manager with strong experience identifying, analysing and documenting business, functional and system requirements. The successful candidate will provide guidance and oversight to the team of business and system analysts, helping to ensure requirements and related deliverables are produced on time, to a high standard and aligned with business priorities. The role will also support the continued adoption and embedding of CLM’s Ways of Working, helping to promote consistent, efficient and effective business analysis practices across the team. The role requires excellent communication and interpersonal skills, together with the ability to work effectively with a diverse group of stakeholders, including senior management, business operations, compliance and technology teams.
This role will report to the Senior Vice President responsible for CLM’s Technology
Responsibilities
Business Analysis
Lead requirements gathering and analysis for CLM projects, enhancements and process improvement initiatives, ensuring business needs are clearly understood and documented.
Prepare and maintain business analysis deliverables, including business requirements, functional specifications, process maps, workflows, user stories, use cases, data requirements and acceptance criteria.
Review and challenge business analysis deliverables, including business requirements, functional specifications, process maps, user stories, acceptance criteria and related documentation, to ensure they are complete, accurate and fit for purpose.
Translate business and regulatory requirements into clear, actionable requirements for technology teams and support solution design discussions to ensure proposed solutions meet business objectives.
Analyse existing business processes, systems and data flows to identify opportunities to simplify ways of working, improve business process, reduce manual effort and enhance the customer experience.
Support the configuration and ongoing support of low-code SaaS applications, engaging with vendors to log, track and follow up on incidents, service requests and enhancement items as required.
Support prioritisation of requirements and backlog items by working with business stakeholders, product owners and technology teams.
Partner with testing and delivery teams to support test planning, review test scenarios, validate that delivered functionality meets requirements and assist with user acceptance testing.
Supervision and Review
Manage and oversee the existing team of Business Analysts, providing day-to-day guidance, direction and support across active projects, enhancements and operational initiatives.
Ensure consistency, quality and appropriate governance of business analysis work across business and technology initiatives, supporting the continued adoption and embedding of automated solutions and ensuring business analysis activity remains aligned with the organisations vision, goals and strategic priorities.
Support prioritisation, resource allocation and workload management across the Business Analysis team, helping to balance technology delivery priorities.
Provide coaching, mentoring and knowledge sharing to develop the capability, confidence and effectiveness of individual Business Analysts.
Monitor progress of business analysis activities against agreed plans and deliverables, identifying risks, dependencies or capacity constraints and escalating where appropriate.
Support regular feedback, performance discussions and development planning for team members in line with business priorities.
Lead release retrospectives and identify process improvement opportunities, leveraging AI, automation and other technology-enabled solutions to improve efficiency, quality and consistency across CLM.
Project & Stakeholder Management
Plan, coordinate and track business analysis activities across multiple technology projects, enhancements and change initiatives, ensuring timelines, dependencies and deliverables are clearly managed.
Work with project managers, product owners, technology teams and business stakeholders to align business analysis activity with agreed delivery plans, priorities and governance requirements.
Identify, manage and escalate risks, issues, assumptions and dependencies relating to business analysis scope, requirements, stakeholder engagement and delivery readiness.
Provide clear and concise progress updates, status reporting and decision-support materials to senior management and key stakeholders.
Build and maintain effective relationships with stakeholders across Operations, Compliance, Technology and other relevant business functions.
Facilitate workshops and meetings with business, compliance, operations and technology stakeholders to define current-state processes, future-state requirements, pain points, risks and opportunities.
Communicate business requirements, solution concepts, impacts and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Qualifications
About You:
You have a degree or equivalent qualification in Business, Technology, Finance, Operations or a related discipline, with a strong interest in financial services, regulatory change and technology-enabled transformation.
You have at least 5 years’ experience in a Business Analysis, Technology, Operations or Financial Services environment.
You have strong business analysis experience, including requirements gathering, process analysis, documentation, stakeholder engagement and supporting technology delivery.
You have experience managing, mentoring or providing oversight to business analysts, system analysts, data analysts or similar roles.
You are able to review and challenge requirements, process maps, user stories, acceptance criteria and related business analysis deliverables to ensure they are clear, complete and fit for purpose.
You possess excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage confidently with senior business, operations, compliance and technology stakeholders.
You can translate complex business, regulatory and technical requirements into clear, practical and actionable documentation.
You are highly organised and able to manage multiple priorities, projects and deliverables in a fast-paced environment.
You can demonstrate strong problem-solving skills, sound judgement and a continuous improvement mindset.
You have experience identifying opportunities to improve processes, reduce manual effort and enhance quality through technology, automation and AI-enabled solutions.
Knowledge of Fenergo/FenX applications or broader CLM, AML/KYC and client due diligence processes is desirable but not essential.
General knowledge of databases, SQL Server, T-SQL, PostgreSQL, APIs or application integration concepts is desirable.
What We Offer
A challenging and rewarding role in an award-winning global business.
Opportunities for personal and professional career development.
Great working environment, competitive salary and benefits, and opportunities for educational support.
Be part of an industry leading global team, renowned

jobs.title: Customer Assistant - Ballincollig Express
jobs.desc:
About the role
We pride ourselves on offering customers the biggest range of products around. And that's not just food, but everything from clothes and kettles to financial services.
But did you know we offer the biggest job opportunities too? With stores across the UK and Ireland, and a variety of roles, we are always looking for people who are as passionate about helping customers as we are.
Our Every Little Helps approach doesn't just apply to our customers. It's at the very heart of everything we do at work - and it's what makes us different. We believe in treating each other with respect, and everyone having the opportunity to get on. That's what makes Tesco such a great place to work.

You will need
Able to give great, natural customer service by proactively smiling, greeting, acknowledging and helping customers.
Works hard for customers, your team and your department.
You are able to prioritise to ensure anything you do is right for our customers.
Adaptable and resilient to meet the ever changing demands of our business.
You must be able to follow instructions either verbal or written.
You are reliable and a good timekeeper.
You must be smart and tidy at all times.
Whats in it for you?
We offer excellent benefits that help make Tesco a great place to work. These include but aren't limited to:
Competitive Salary
Bonus Scheme*
Our Virtual GP service provides free and confidential access to an online GP through video GP consultations, and online prescription service for colleagues. The service is also available to families of colleagues who live at the same address for a reduced cost.
24/7 access to our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) for you and family members for in the moment emotional support along with free access to a range of wellbeing services supporting you under our new Wellbeing First approach of Body, Mind and Life.
Colleague Clubcard offering 10% discount across stores and online, with 15% discount weekends once a month (Friday to Sunday), and 20% off twice a year. There is also 20% off F&F clothing, all year long, these various discounts can be extended to a family member with a 2nd Clubcard available.*
Life Assurance
Pension Plan*
Save As You Earn Scheme*
Paid Family Leave
Bike to Work
Long Service Awards
Commuter Scheme
*Entry requirements and rules of the scheme apply
About Us
Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer's favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move. Our core purpose is "Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day". Serving means more than a transactional relationship with our customers. It means acting as a responsible and sustainable business for all stakeholders, for the communities we are part of, and for the planet. Through initiatives like the Tesco Community Fund, our association with Children's Health Foundation, our partnership with FoodCloud and our Stronger Starts programme, we have supported over 21,000 community groups, raised over €7.5 million for medical equipment, and provided almost 15 million meals nationwide, to those living in food insecurity.
Tesco has operated in the Irish retail market since 1997, and with 190+ stores nationwide, we employ over 13,000 people in cities and towns around Ireland, supporting almost 45,000 jobs directly and indirectly. We partner with over 500 Irish suppliers - of which almost three-quarters are small and medium enterprises - which in turn supports almost 13,000 farming families around Ireland. Tesco is the single largest buyer of Irish food and drink in the world, buying €1.6 Billion a year; more than any other single country in the European Union, more than even the USA which you perceive as a massive buyer of Irish food.
We work closely with suppliers across Ireland who are dedicated to making the best products for our customers and this is reflected in the numerous awards our products have won over the years including Blás Na hÉireann, World Steak Challenge and Great Taste Awards.
We are proud to have an inclusive culture at Tesco where everyone truly feels able to be themselves. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated. At Tesco, we not only celebrate diversity, but recognise the value and opportunity it brings. We always want our colleagues to feel they can be themselves at work and we are committed to helping them be at their best.
We know life looks a little different for each of us. That's why at Tesco, we always welcome chats about flexible working. Some people are at the start of their careers, some want the freedom to do the things they love. Others are going through life-changing moments like becoming a carer, nearing retirement, adapting to parenthood, or something else. So, talk to us throughout your application about how we can support.
Tesco is committed to celebrating diversity and everyone is welcome at Tesco. We're committed to providing a fully inclusive recruitment process, allowing candidates the opportunity to thrive and inform us of any reasonable adjustments they may require. For further information on the accessibility support we can offer, please click http://roi.tesco-careers.com/accessibility/
How can I let Tesco know I need additional support?
Please let us know you need additional support by emailing tescoireland.recruitment@tesco.ie
This will allow us to understand more about you and how we can best support you through the recruitment process.

jobs.title: Global Operational Technology Engineer
jobs.desc:
Overview
PepsiCo is on the look-out for a Global Operational Technology Engineer to join our global engineering function.
We are the concentrate business in PepsiCo (PGCS) working across the Beverage, Nutrition and Snacks categories to deliver concentrate for many of PepsiCo’s mega brands including Gatorade, 7Up and Pepsi. We are at the heart of PepsiCo products consumed everywhere in the world, spanning globally sourcing ingredients to manufacturing and distributing across the globe PGCS is a multi-functional business unit offering careers in various functions from Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Procurement, Quality, Finance, Tax, Customs & Trade, R&D, HR and IT. We want team members who can collaborate in our fast-paced global organisation and are passionate about creating and delivering much-loved household brands to markets across the world.
The Technical Function is our team of enabling experts offering knowledge and partnership to functions on specialist subjects including engineering, quality and productivity. They ensure operations and food safety excellence for our team. Could you bring a new dimension to our technical expertise? If so we could take your talents to a whole new level.
This role is a global role based in Cork, reporting to the Global Operational Technology Lead, this is a central engineering role.
Responsibilities
This role will support the delivery, integration and sustainment of Operational Technology systems across PGCS sites globally, with a strong focus on AVEVA-based platforms and MES-enabled manufacturing. The position plays a key role in ensuring reliable data exchange between automation and enterprise layers while driving standardisation, cybersecurity compliance and long-term supportability of OT solutions.Key responsibilities include:
Support the delivery of MES batching projects from an automation and OT integration perspective.
Ensure Digital Factory initiatives have the required automation data points, connectivity and contextualisation to enable reliable MES ↔ Automation communication.
Configure, deploy and sustain AVEVA System Platform, OMI, InTouch and InBatch solutions across multiple sites.
Develop and maintain integration mechanisms between PLCs, System Platform and MES layers, including SQL-based data handling and validation.
Support global migration, standardisation and template strategy for AVEVA System Platform implementations.
Work closely with system integrators and vendors to ensure solutions align with PGCS OT standards and cybersecurity requirements.
Provide technical governance to ensure projects comply with PepsiCo automation specifications, GAMP principles and industry best practice.
Contribute to OT cybersecurity readiness, including secure architecture, patching strategies and access control alignment with corporate standards.
Support incident management, troubleshooting and lifecycle sustainment of OT platforms across global sites.
Assist in developing and maintaining OT standards, documentation and approved design patterns.
Deliver knowledge transfer and technical training to site teams to ensure successful operational handover.
Engage collaboratively with global stakeholders across Engineering, IT, Digital Factory and Supply Chain functions.
Standardisation & Training
Ensure all OT implementations follow PGCS global automation standards and approved design frameworks.
Drive consistency in System Platform configuration, deployment models and integration approaches across sites.
Provide technical training and mentoring to site engineering teams to support adoption and sustainment of deployed solutions.
Support development of reusable templates, documentation and best practices for global rollout.
Qualifications
Strong hands-on experience with: AVEVA System Platform
AVEVA OMI
AVEVA InTouch
AVEVA InBatch
AVEVA MES integrations
Experience using SQL within industrial environments for data management and troubleshooting.
Proven experience delivering OT / automation solutions within manufacturing environments.
Experience managing system integrators and automation vendors.
Understanding of OT cybersecurity principles and secure industrial architectures.
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Automation, Computer Science or related discipline.
Typically 5 to 10 years’ experience in a similar industrial role.
Experience working within GAMP or regulated manufacturing environments preferred.
Strong stakeholder engagement, documentation and communication skills.
Degree in Automation, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science or related discipline.
Typically 5 to 10 years’ experience in industrial automation or OT roles.
Experience working within regulated or GAMP-aligned environments preferred.
Strong communication, documentation and stakeholder engagement skills.
Additional Qualifications And/or Experience
Experience supporting global digital transformation programmes.
Exposure to standardisation of plant models, templates and multi-site architectures.
Familiarity with lifecycle management and sustainment of OT platforms at scale.
PepsiCo products are enjoyed by consumers more than one billion times a day in more than 200 countries and territories around the world. PepsiCo generated more than $79 billion in net revenue in 2021, driven by a complementary beverage and convenient foods portfolio that includes Lay’s, Doritos, Cheetos, Gatorade, Pepsi-Cola, Mountain Dew, Quaker, and SodaStream. PepsiCo's product portfolio includes a wide range of enjoyable foods and beverages, including many iconic brands that generate more than $1 billion each in estimated annual retail sales.
For the purposes of external advertising we have called this role Global Operational Technology Engineer. However please note that the internal job title the successful candidate will be Process Eng Engineer.

Stepping Ahead Clinic values a supportive, professional environment where clinicians can grow their skills while making a meaningful impact on children and families in the community.
Role Description
This is a full-time, on-site Occupational Therapist role based in County Cork, Ireland. The Occupational Therapist will conduct comprehensive assessments of children and young people, develop individualized intervention plans, and deliver evidence-based therapy sessions within the clinic’s centers. Daily tasks include collaborating with the multidisciplinary team, maintaining accurate clinical documentation, and communicating progress and recommendations to caregivers, schools, and other stakeholders. The role also involves contributing to group programs, supporting MDT Autism assessments, and participating in team meetings, case discussions, and service development initiatives. The Occupational Therapist is expected to uphold ethical practice, safeguard client wellbeing, and engage in ongoing professional development.
Qualifications
Candidates should possess strong skills in Occupational Therapy, including assessment, intervention planning, and outcome measurement for children and young people.
Candidates should possess excellent Communication skills, including clear written documentation, collaborative teamwork, and the ability to explain therapeutic goals and strategies to families and caregivers.
Recognised degree or postgraduate qualification in Occupational Therapy and current professional CORU registration.
Experience working with pediatric populations in clinical, educational, or community settings, ideally including autism and neurodevelopmental conditions.
Ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary team and to manage a caseload in a structured, organised manner.
Commitment to evidence-based practice, continuous learning, and participation in clinical supervision and professional development.
Strong problem-solving skills, cultural sensitivity, and a client-centered approach that respects diversity and individual needs.

About the role
At Tesco, we see the value in you –and right now we are hiring Customer Delivery Drivers to join our team
Our core purpose is to serve Irish shoppers a little better every day and being a
Customer Delivery Driver
you are the first face our customers see.
Being a Customer Delivery Driver is hands on, physical and full of variety. No two shifts are ever the same – customer’s look for help in all kinds of different ways.
For most of the day you’ll feel like your own boss, delivering to your customers but with a team of managers and colleagues back at base ready to support you when you need them.
Shift Pattern:
Various shifts available
You will be responsible for
Providing an excellent home shopping experience by putting our customers at the heart of everything we do is our main responsibility.
Loading the van where required, and check your van for roadworthines
Understanding the schedule and route that has been calculated for you
Looking the part in your uniform, ready to help our customers
Driving safely, responsibly and within the law
To be courteous to all road users
Serving your customer with a smile and greet them by name
Taking care of your customer’s deliveries as if they were your own
You will need
To have had a full IRISH or EU driving licence (manual or automatic) for at least 2 years with no more than 3 penalty points
To be a safe and courteous drivers
To enjoy helping others
To be personable with a good sense of humour and excellent communication skills
The ability to take the initiative and use common sense
To care about making a difference for customers and colleagues
The ability to stay calm under pressure
Please be aware that as part of our recruitment process, job offers are subject to the Garda Vetting Process and you will need to provide proof of current penalty points on your licence at Assessment Stage. This can be requested from the National Driver Licence Services (NDLS) on
1890 41 61 41. Press Option 4 and quote your driver number.
We are sorry but if you have been disqualified from driving within the last 10 years, we will not be able to accept your application.
Should you be successful in your application, your offer will be subject to and conditional upon you providing your bank account details before your agreed start date.
Whats in it for you?
We offer excellent benefits that help make Tesco a great place to work. These include but aren’t limited to:
A variety of shifts
Part time and full time contracts available between 20 -  39 hours   a week
An hourly rate of pay for new drivers of €18.24 per hour with additional premium for Sunday working
Annual Bonus Scheme
Colleague Clubcard offering 10% discount across stores and online, with 15% discount weekends once a month (Friday to Sunday), and 20% off twice a year. There is also 20% off F&F clothing, all year long, these various discounts can be extended to a family member with a 2
nd
Clubcard available.*
Our Virtual GP service provides free and confidential access to an online GP through video GP consultations, and online prescription service for colleagues. The service is also available to families of colleagues who live at the same address for a reduced cost.
24/7 access to our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) for you and family members for in the moment emotional support along with free access to a range of wellbeing services supporting you under our new Wellbeing First approach of Body, Mind and Life.
Life Assurance
Pension Plan*
Save As You Earn Scheme*
Paid Family Leave
Bike to Work
Long Service Awards
Commuter Scheme
*Entry requirements and rules of the scheme apply
About Us
Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer’s favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move.  Our core purpose is “Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day”.  Serving means more than a transactional relationship with our customers.  It means acting as a responsible and sustainable business for all stakeholders, for the communities we are part of, and for the planet. Through initiatives like the Tesco Community Fund, our association with Children’s Health Foundation, our partnership with FoodCloud and our Stronger Starts programme, we have supported over 21,000 community groups, raised over €7.5 million for medical equipment, and provided almost 15 million meals nationwide, to those living in food insecurity.
Tesco has operated in the Irish retail market since 1997, and with 190+ stores nationwide, we employ over 13,000 people in cities and towns around Ireland, supporting almost 45,000 jobs directly and indirectly. We partner with over 500 Irish suppliers - of which almost three-quarters are small and medium enterprises - which in turn supports almost 13,000 farming families around Ireland. Tesco is the single largest buyer of Irish food and drink in the world, buying €1.6 Billion a year; more than any other single country in the European Union, more than even the USA which you perceive as a massive buyer of Irish food.
We work closely with suppliers across Ireland who are dedicated to making the best products for our customers and this is reflected in the numerous awards our products have won over the years including Blás Na hÉireann, World Steak Challenge and Great Taste Awards.
We are proud to have an inclusive culture at Tesco where everyone truly feels able to be themselves. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated.   At Tesco, we not only celebrate diversity, but recognise the value and opportunity it brings.  We always want our colleagues to feel they can be themselves at work and we are committed to helping them be at their best.
We know life looks a little different for each of us. That’s why at Tesco, we always welcome chats about flexible working. Some people are at the start of their careers, some want the freedom to do the things they love. Others are going through life-changing moments like becoming a carer, nearing retirement, adapting to parenthood, or something else. So, talk to us throughout your application about how we can support.
Tesco is committed to celebrating diversity and everyone is welcome at Tesco. We're committed to providing a fully inclusive recruitment process, allowing candidates the opportunity to thrive and inform us of any reasonable adjustments they may require. For further information on the accessibility support we can offer, please click http://roi.tesco-careers.com/accessibility/

tescoireland.recruitment@tesco.ie

jobs.title: Manager, Engineering
jobs.desc:
About Advanced Energy
Advanced Energy (Nasdaq: AEIS) is a global leader in the design and manufacturing of highly engineered, precision power conversion, measurement and control solutions for mission-critical applications and processes. AE’s power solutions enable customer innovation in complex applications for a wide range of industries including semiconductor equipment, industrial, manufacturing, telecommunications, data center computing and healthcare.
With engineering know-how and responsive service and support around the globe, the company builds collaborative partnerships to meet technology advances, propel growth for its customers and innovate the future of power. Advanced Energy has devoted four decades to perfecting power for its global customers and is headquartered in Denver, Colorado.
Our site in Little Island, Cork, Ireland is seeking an Engineering Manager to join our Future Technologies team!
Position Summary
As Engineering Manager, Future Technologies, you will guide and grow a talented team of engineers developing innovative power solutions that make life-changing therapies possible. From concept through commercialization, you will drive the creation of new-to-world technologies that help medical device leaders bring safer, more effective, and more connected treatments to patients worldwide. This position sits at the forefront of innovation, leading the development of disruptive technologies that will power tomorrow's medical devices. You will work on ambitious, first-of-their-kind designs, transforming emerging concepts into products that enable groundbreaking advances in surgery, diagnostics, and therapeutic care.
The Engineering Manager, Future Technologies will lead the development of strategic technology platforms that enable emerging medical applications and breakthrough treatments. Working closely with customers, product management, and advanced development teams, you will build and lead an organization focused on solving complex technical challenges and delivering innovations that improve patient outcomes globally.
For an ambitious engineering leader, this is an opportunity to accelerate your career by leading highly visible, strategic development programs that are expected to define the next generation of our medical product portfolio. You will have the chance to influence technology strategy, develop future leaders, and expand your impact across a global organization.
Responsibilities
Lead the team in the development of next-generation power technologies that enable breakthrough medical devices, therapies, and treatment modalities.
Drive the identification, evaluation, and maturation of emerging technologies, transforming innovative concepts into commercially successful products.
Foster a culture of technical curiosity, experimentation, and continuous innovation, encouraging the team to challenge conventional approaches and push technological boundaries.
Act as a visible technical leader within the organization, influencing architectural decisions, platform strategies, and future product investments.
Identify and cultivate future technical and people leaders, strengthening the organization's engineering capability and succession pipeline.
Drive a high-performance culture that balances innovation, accountability, collaboration, and execution excellence.
Collaborate with customers to solve complex technical challenges and develop solutions that create competitive advantage.

Honours Degree in Electrical / Electronic Engineering or equivalent.
8 years' minimum experience in an electronics development environment.
Minimum 5 years' previous experience in leading/managing engineering projects and engineering teams.
Proven leadership experience.
Proven experience in developing and executing to project budgets.
Proven innovation in technology and intellectual property.

Onsite at our Little Island, Cork, Ireland facility.
The role will also include domestic and international travel of up to 20%.

Summary
At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish. The people here at Apple donʼt just create products — they create the kind of wonder thatʼs revolutionised entire industries. Itʼs the diversity of those people and their ideas that inspires innovation that runs through everything we do, from amazing technology to industry-leading environmental efforts. Join Apple and help us enrich lives and leave the world in a better place than we found it!
The Finance department based in the Cork Campus supports all functions of Apple in EMEIA, including the European Sales Fulfilment, AppleCare after-sales services, European Logistics, Manufacturing & Operations, Apple Media Products, Apple Retail as well as being the Shared Services Centre for EMEIA.
Description
Engineering & Operations Finance partners with the Engineering, Operations, and AppleCare teams to optimize the world’s most innovative supply chain and provide the best possible customer experience. Intricately connected with their business partners, Engineering & Operations Finance provides analysis for insightful decision making. The team is located in five major global sites: Cupertino, Austin, Shanghai, Singapore, and Cork.
This 15 month role is in the Operations Finance team, reporting directly to the Tooling / FP&A Finance Manager. Each Analyst as part of the team is primarily responsible for the management of costs and controls within a specified business area. The team interfaces directly with the key stakeholders, which includes Product Operations, Supply Demand Management (SDM), Logistics, GBS and Ops Finance, Technical Accounting, Tax and several other Operations groups.
There are 7 members working in the FP&A Finance team. Each team member actively engages with and supports key business partners within the local business teams to provide analytical & decision-making support, as well as being responsible for quarter end close & forecasting activities within their function.
You will have great exposure within the Operations Finance team, the wider Finance org and at the Executive Operations level in EMEIA and beyond. If you are analytical and skilled at building phenomenal working relationships, then this position is an exciting opportunity for you!
Responsibilities
Strategic Business Partnering: Serve as the strategic finance partner for Product Operations, overseeing iMac manufacturing in Cork and Value Add Services across EMEIA Distribution Centres; drive quarterly cost reviews, build metrics packs, and model financial impacts for new business opportunities.
P&L Ownership & FP&A: Own the EMEIA OCOGS P&L through comprehensive financial planning and analysis, including forecasting, actuals reporting, and quarter-end close deliverables (JVs, BSRs, and flux analysis).
Executive Reviews & Metrics: Lead quarterly business reviews with senior Operations and Finance leaders, delivering critical management reporting and KPIs that illuminate cost drivers and inform executive decisions.
Operational Leadership Support: Deliver high-touch financial guidance to EMEIA Operations Directors and the broader finance leadership team, proactively identifying opportunities to expand scope and provide ad-hoc strategic analysis.
Sustainability & Profitability: Champion cost-reduction and revenue-generating initiatives while playing an active role in advancing Apple's 2030 carbon neutrality and sustainability commitments.
Global Collaboration: Partner with regional finance teams globally to design, align, and roll out strategic operational initiatives that scale across Apple worldwide.
Governance & Controls: Safeguard financial integrity by maintaining Apple's internal control standards across all business interactions, financial models, and accounting workflows.
Innovation & Tooling: Leverage modern AI tools, automation technologies, and advanced financial systems to enhance workflows, drive efficiencies, and uncover deeper business insights.
Minimum Qualifications
Proven track record in FP&A, commercial finance, or operational accounting roles.
Strong technical and financial modeling capabilities, with demonstrated expertise in managing large data sets, driving reporting efficiencies, and synthesizing complex findings into actionable executive summaries.
Thorough grounding in core financial processes, including P&L forecasting, variance analysis, and month-end/quarter-end close procedures.
Outstanding communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to connect authentically, challenge assumptions constructively, and influence cross-functional partners.
Demonstrated ability to thrive and deliver excellence in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
Natural curiosity and a disciplined, analytical approach to problem-solving, with comfort operating through ambiguity.
High level of personal resilience, candour, and positive energy, paired with an appetite for continuous process improvement and change management.
Preferred Qualifications
Prior experience in operations finance, supply chain, or manufacturing environments (particularly with OCOGS or distribution network cost accounting).
Experience operating within a large, matrixed multinational organization, with a track record of driving cross-regional initiatives.
Hands-on familiarity or strong enthusiasm for adopting generative AI tools, automation workflows, and advanced data visualization platforms (e.g., Tableau) within a finance context.
Recognized professional finance/accounting qualification (such as ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CPA) or an advanced degree (e.g., Master's or MBA).
Experience presenting financial strategy directly to senior operational directors and business unit heads.

Summary
Apple's Strategic Data Solutions (SDS) team is seeking a hands-on, self-motivated Software Engineering Manager to deliver cutting-edge analytical solutions with enhanced user experience. Our mission is Enterprise Decision Automation, protecting Apple and our customers from fraud, waste, and abuse. Your contributions will be pivotal to our success.
Do you thrive on solving complex challenges with direct, meaningful impact? Are you passionate about building tools and systems that enable data analysis over petabytes of data?
Do you want to work alongside talented Data Scientists, Machine Learning Engineers, Software Engineers, Program Managers, and Apple business partners? If so, we'd love to have you on our team!
Description
With the expansive data we have, our job is to build meaningful tools and solutions that empower our internal partners and drive fraud prevention across Apple. The Solutions SWE team is a global, cross-LOB (line-of-business) engineering team focused on four core areas: efficiency solutions, internal tooling, operational excellence, and direct LOB support.
As the Engineering Manager for Solutions SWE, you will directly lead and grow a team of 5-6 Software Engineers based in Cork, Ireland (EMEA), while contributing to the broader functional roadmap across regions. You will balance hands-on technical leadership with people management, developing talent, and partnering with fraud investigators, analysts, engineers, product managers, and business partners to ship solutions that solve real business problems.
Responsibilities
Directly managing, coaching, and growing the engineering team in Cork, including hiring, performance management, and career development
Contributing to the functional and technical roadmap for Solutions SWE, in partnership with regional counterparts
Partnering with fraud investigators, analysts, product managers, and business partners to gather requirements, set priorities, and deliver outcomes
Ensuring the team ships reliable, scalable production software and automation that reduces manual work across operations, analytics, and engineering
Owning delivery end-to-end from planning and development through deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement
Coordinating across time zones and regional teams to keep a distributed organization aligned and effective
Partnering with the broader SWE organization to align on technical patterns and grow the engineering craft of the team
Minimum Qualifications
3+ years leading software engineers, either as a people manager or as a technical lead who directed the day-to-day work of a team of at least 3 engineers
Hands-on experience writing and shipping production software in Python, Java, or a comparable language, with code contributions in the last 2 years
Experience owning delivery end to end, from planning and development through deployment, monitoring and iteration
Experience working with non-engineering partners (for example product, operations, analysts or business stakeholders) to gather requirements and agree priorities
Experience working with teams spread across multiple locations or time zones
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with or exposure to machine learning, useful for partnering with MLEs

Proven experience as a Bricklaying Foreman, Lead Bricklayer or similar supervisory role on residential, commercial, industrial or large-scale construction projects.

Excellent leadership and communication skills, with the ability to motivate teams and build strong working relationships with site management, clients and subcontractors.

About the Role:
As an integral member of Logitech Finance, you will work in a fast-paced, dynamic Global Payroll team processing payrolls across the Americas region — covering the United States, Canada, and Latin America. Your Contribution:
Be Yourself. Be Open. Stay Hungry and Humble. Collaborate. Challenge. Decide and Do.
In this role you will:
Ensure the accurate and timely processing of Logitech’s end-to-end payroll for the AMR region (USA, Canada, and LATAM).
Collaborate with payroll partners to collect and validate all payroll inputs, including salaries, bonuses, benefits, allowances, and deductions. Conduct rigorous pre- and post-payroll reconciliations to eliminate anomalies or duplicate records before finalization.
Ensure the accurate and timely completion of payroll fiscal close procedures, including journal entries and balance sheet reconciliations. Work with the broader Finance team to identify and resolve payroll accounting exceptions.
Understand the full payroll cycle through to GL bookings and present meaningful flux analysis to stakeholders.
Stay current on and ensure strict compliance with federal, state/provincial, and local payroll regulations, tax laws, social security, and benefits requirements across all AMR jurisdictions.
Ensure compliance with payroll internal controls, maintaining robust documentation and proactively identifying and remediating any control gaps or weaknesses. Assist in facilitating internal and external audit engagements.
Partner with key stakeholders including People Services, HRIS, Compensation & Benefits, Stock Admin, and Finance to troubleshoot issues and work collaboratively to develop optimum processes and service delivery.
Drive the payroll Global Finance Transformation roadmap, focusing on eliminating manual workflows and implementing scalable, automated payroll solutions.
Collaborate with internal and external partners to drive automation and enhance service delivery.
Your Skills & Experience:
Beyond core technical payroll knowledge, we are seeking an innovative, highly data-literate payroll professional who actively identifies opportunities to leverage modern tools, AI, and emerging technologies to automate workflows and transform end-to-end payroll operations.
For consideration, you must bring the following skills, experience and behaviours to our team:
Experience: 3+ years of proven experience in a senior analyst payroll role, specifically working with Americas payroll (US required; Canada and LATAM experience is a major plus).
Education & Certification: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or a related field—or an equivalent payroll certification.
Regulatory Compliance: Solid understanding of US/Canadian payroll taxes, statutory deductions, and labour regulations.
Hands-on experience processing payroll and running reports in Workday and/or Dayforce (Ceridian).
Spreadsheet Skills: Advanced proficiency in MS Excel and Google Sheets (must be comfortable using Pivot Tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, and managing large data sets).
Familiarity with how HRIS data flows into downstream payroll and Finance/GL systems.
Strong ability to perform pre- and post-payroll reconciliations, investigate gross-to-net variances, and flag data errors before finalization.
Experience supporting month-end close procedures, including preparing journal entries and assisting Finance/FP&A teams with cost analysis.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills to partner effectively across HR, Finance, and external vendors.
Ability to stay organized and solve problems independently in a fast-paced, global team environment.
Customer service focus with the ability and sound judgment to handle highly sensitive information.
Process improvement mindset: have a passion for reengineering payroll processes in implementing a first-class payroll service.
Strong interest in applying emerging technologies—such as AI, ML, and RPA—to re-engineer enterprise payroll workflows, eliminate manual touchpoints, and unlock value-added insights for workforce planning.
About Logitech
With a fast-moving, innovative culture and a strong balance sheet, Logitech is a world leader in products that connect people to the digital experiences they care most about. Video conferencing, remote work, content creation, and gaming are long-term secular trends driving our business — and today all of them have accelerated, making Logitech more relevant to customers than ever.
Logitech is the sweet spot for people who are passionate about products, making a mark, and having fun doing it. We're small and flexible enough for every person to take initiative — and big enough for those actions to have a global impact.
Across Logitech we empower collaboration and foster play. We help teams collaborate/learn from anywhere, without compromising on productivity or continuity so it should be no surprise that most of our jobs are open to work from home from most locations. Our hybrid work model allows some employees to work remotely while others work on-premises. Within this structure, you may have teams or departments split between working remotely and working in-house.
Logitech is an amazing place to work because it is full of authentic people who are inclusive by nature as well as by design. Being a global company, we value our diversity and celebrate all our differences. Don’t meet every single requirement? Not a problem. If you feel you are the right candidate for the opportunity, we strongly recommend that you apply. We want to meet you!
We offer comprehensive and competitive benefits packages and working environments that are designed to be flexible and help you to care for yourself and your loved ones, now and in the future. We believe that good health means more than getting medical care when you need it. Logitech supports a culture that encourages individuals to achieve good physical, financial, emotional, intellectual and social wellbeing so we all can create, achieve and enjoy more and support our families. We can’t wait to tell you more about them being that there are too many to list here and they vary based on location.

But did you know we offer the biggest job opportunities too? With stores across the UK and Ireland, and a variety of roles, we are always looking for people who are as passionate about helping customers as we are.
Our Every Little Helps approach doesn't just apply to our customers. It's at the very heart of everything we do at work - and it's what makes us different. We believe in treating each other with respect, and everyone having the opportunity to get on. That's what makes Tesco such a great place to work.

We offer excellent benefits that help make Tesco a great place to work. These include but aren't limited to:
Competitive Salary

24/7 access to our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) for you and family members for in the moment emotional support along with free access to a range of wellbeing services supporting you under our new Wellbeing First approach of Body, Mind and Life.

Pension Plan*
Save As You Earn Scheme*

Bike to Work
Long Service Awards
Commuter Scheme

About Us
Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer's favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move. Our core purpose is "Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day". Serving means more than a transactional relationship with our customers. It means acting as a responsible and sustainable business for all stakeholders, for the communities we are part of, and for the planet. Through initiatives like the Tesco Community Fund, our association with Children's Health Foundation, our partnership with FoodCloud and our Stronger Starts programme, we have supported over 21,000 community groups, raised over €7.5 million for medical equipment, and provided almost 15 million meals nationwide, to those living in food insecurity.
Tesco has operated in the Irish retail market since 1997, and with 190+ stores nationwide, we employ over 13,000 people in cities and towns around Ireland, supporting almost 45,000 jobs directly and indirectly. Tesco is the single largest buyer of Irish food and drink in the world, buying €1.6 Billion a year; more than any other single country in the European Union, more than even the USA which you perceive as a massive buyer of Irish food.
We work closely with suppliers across Ireland who are dedicated to making the best products for our customers and this is reflected in the numerous awards our products have won over the years including Blás Na hÉireann, World Steak Challenge and Great Taste Awards.
We are proud to have an inclusive culture at Tesco where everyone truly feels able to be themselves. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated. At Tesco, we not only celebrate diversity, but recognise the value and opportunity it brings. We always want our colleagues to feel they can be themselves at work and we are committed to helping them be at their best.
We know life looks a little different for each of us. That's why at Tesco, we always welcome chats about flexible working. So, talk to us throughout your application about how we can support.
Tesco is committed to celebrating diversity and everyone is welcome at Tesco. jobs.title: Civil Engineer - Water Networks
jobs.desc:
The Opportunity
THE OPPORTUNITY
This is an opportunity to join Stantec’s growing water sector team in Ireland, where you will contribute to the delivery of critical infrastructure that supports communities, protects the environment, and addresses the challenges of climate change. As a Civil Engineer, you will work on a diverse range of water and wastewater projects, from concept and feasibility through to detailed design and construction support, gaining exposure across the full project lifecycle.
You will be part of a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment, working alongside experts in engineering, environmental science, and planning to deliver integrated and sustainable solutions. The role offers the chance to build your technical expertise in areas such as network design, treatment processes, and asset management, while also developing your project management and client-facing skills
About The Role
As a Civil Engineer in Stantec’s water team, you will support the delivery of water and wastewater projects across all stages, from concept to construction. You will contribute to technical design work, including drawings, calculations, and specifications, while assisting with reports and contract documentation.
Working within a multidisciplinary team, you will collaborate with engineers, environmental specialists, and project managers, gaining broad project experience and exposure to clients and stakeholders. This role offers a strong platform to develop your technical skills and grow your career within Ireland’s water sector.
YOUR IMPACT
In this role, you will contribute to the delivery of essential water and wastewater infrastructure that supports communities, public health, and environmental protection across Ireland. Your work will help ensure reliable water services, improve network performance, and enhance resilience to climate change.
By applying sound engineering principles and attention to detail, you will support the development of practical, efficient, and sustainable design solutions. Your input will help projects meet regulatory requirements, reduce environmental impact, and deliver long-term value for clients and stakeholders.
Through collaboration with multidisciplinary teams, you will play a part in driving high-quality project outcomes, strengthening client relationships, and supporting the continued growth and reputation of Stantec in Ireland’s water sector.
About You
You are a qualified Civil Engineer with a strong technical foundation and proven experience in water network design. You bring a practical, solutions-focused mindset and are comfortable working both independently and as part of a collaborative, multidisciplinary team.
You Will Demonstrate
A minimum Level 8 degree in Engineering (or a related discipline)
Strong post-graduate experience in water network design
Solid professional and technical knowledge, with the ability to apply engineering principles effectively
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage with colleagues and clients
WHY JOIN US
We put people first: We're proud of our friendly, inclusive and collaborative environment where everyone feels valued and driven to succeed.
We are driven to achieve: Named in the top 50 companies to work by Glassdoor 2025. Recognised by Corporate Knights as one of the world's top 10 most sustainable companies 2025. =
We do what is right: Industry leading training and development as well as paid for professional subscriptions. A professional progression plan, supporting you to become chartered.
We are better together: A supportive and collaborative team environment to assist with the growth of your career.
Growth: We're on an exciting growth journey across the Ireland - we want you to be part of it!
Great Benefits: Competitive salary, enhanced pension plan, annual leave with the option to buy/sell additional days, private medical insurance, group income protection & life assurance included as standard!
About Stantec
Whether you’re starting out on your engineering career or are looking for a fresh challenge, Ryan Hanley, now part of Stantec, is a great career move.
Based in Dublin, Galway, Castlebar and Cork, we are actively recruiting for team players with experience in any of the following areas – water and wastewater treatment process and network design, integrated network management, structural design, site development, road and bridge engineering, project management and administration.
You’ll be working for a dynamic company with an excellent reputation in the industry.
Ryan Hanley, now part of Stantec, offers a great working environment amongst friendly professionals with an emphasis on teamwork. It’s a company where your ideas and opinions will be valued and your efforts recognised and rewarded.
We have been awarded the silver Investors in Diversity accreditation by the Irish Centre for Diversity for our commitment to quality, diversity and inclusion (EDI) in the workplace.

jobs.title: Design Manager (Design & Build)
jobs.desc:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.
Your impact
You will help turn some of the UK & Ireland's most important water and wastewater plans into safe, buildable and effective infrastructure.
Working across multidisciplinary programmes, you will bring engineering disciplines, construction teams and client stakeholders together around clear, coordinated design decisions. You will help identify risks early, improve buildability and make sure commissioning, operational performance and whole-life value are considered throughout the design process.
This is a role for an experienced engineering professional who understands how complex designs move from development into delivery. You will coordinate technical interfaces, manage design information and help project teams resolve issues before they affect construction, programme or cost.
You will work closely with project managers, technical specialists and construction teams, providing design management support and giving clients confidence that designs are coordinated, assured and ready for delivery.
Your contribution will go beyond managing drawings and schedules. You will challenge assumptions, support better ways of working and help teams make practical decisions that improve safety, value and long-term performance.
About The Opportunity
The UK water sector is entering a significant period of investment, creating the opportunity to improve the resilience, capacity and environmental performance of critical infrastructure.
As a Design Manager, you will coordinate multidisciplinary detailed design activities across water and wastewater projects and programmes. You will work with civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, process and construction teams to produce integrated, buildable designs that support successful delivery, commissioning and operation.
You will take day-to-day responsibility for defined design packages or project workstreams, helping manage scope, programme, technical interfaces, assurance requirements and design change. Working alongside senior design managers, project managers and discipline leads, you will track progress, coordinate inputs and help resolve technical or delivery issues.
You will also work closely with construction and commissioning teams to make sure buildability, sequencing, access, safety and operational requirements are reflected in the design. Where opportunities exist, you will support the use of standardised solutions, digital tools and lessons learned to improve design efficiency and consistency.
Depending on the size and complexity of the programme, you may coordinate a small design team or manage several technical packages within a larger multidisciplinary delivery environment. You will provide clear direction and constructive support, but you will not be expected to carry the same practice leadership, business development or people-management responsibilities as a Senior Design Manager.
This is a great opportunity to join a growing water practice and take on greater responsibility across complex infrastructure programmes. Success will mean improving design coordination, identifying risk early and helping multidisciplinary teams produce engineering solutions that work in design, construction and operation.
This role can be based out of several locations across our major UK & Ireland offices
Here's what you'll need
We would be delighted to hear from and speak to candidates with a progressive mix of the following
Experience coordinating the design or engineering delivery of water, wastewater or comparable infrastructure projects within a consultancy, contractor, delivery partner or asset-owner environment.
Evidence of managing defined design packages or project workstreams, including design scope, programme, technical interfaces, deliverables, assurance activities and change.
Practical understanding of how engineering design interacts with construction, commissioning, operations and maintenance
Working knowledge of Design & Build contracts and CDM requirements, helping teams identify, record and manage design risk.
Experience working within NEC3 or NEC4 delivery environments, including an understanding of change control, early warnings and the relationship between design decisions, programme and cost.
We offer
Competitive salary We offer compensation that reflects your skills and experience
Flexible Work Arrangements Benefit from hybrid, part-time, and flexible working hours, patterns, and locations
Robust Pension Contributions We offer enhanced pension contributions up to 10% to secure your future
Comprehensive Health Coverage Single medical cover and Digital GP service, with options to add your partner and family
Family Planning Support Access to fertility healthcare and family planning services
Enhanced Parental Leave Enjoy enhanced parental leave pay and free membership to employee assistance and parental programs
Life assurance at 4x your salary
Wellbeing Hub Free access to wellbeing apps like Calm and Daily Burn
Professional Development We cover professional membership fees and provide continuous professional development (CPD) opportunities
Community Engagement Participate in charity matched-funding, paid volunteering time, and charitable donations
#Design #Water #Infrastructure
Joining Jacobs not only connects you locally but globally. Our values stand on a foundation of safety, integrity, inclusion and belonging. We put people at the heart of our business, and we truly believe that by supporting one another through our culture of caring, we all succeed. We value positive mental health and a sense of belonging for all employees.
With safety and flexibility always top of mind, we’ve gone beyond traditional ways of working so you have the support, means and space to maximize your potential. You’ll uncover flexible working arrangements, benefits, and opportunities, from well-being benefits to our global giving and volunteering program, to exploring new and inventive ways to help our clients make the world a better place. No matter what drives you, you’ll discover how you can cultivate, nurture, and achieve your goals – all at a single global company. Find out more about life at Jacobs.
We aim to embed inclusion and belonging in everything we do. We know that if we are inclusive, we’re more connected and creative. We accept people for who they are, and we champion the richness of different perspectives, lived experiences and backgrounds in the workplace, as a source of learning and innovation. We are committed to building vibrant communities within Jacobs, including through our Jacobs Employee Networks, Communities of Practice and our Find Your Community initiatives, allowing every employee to find connection, purpose, and belonging. Find out more about our Jacobs Employee Networks here.

About the role
At Tesco, we see the value in you –and right now we are hiring Customer Delivery Drivers to join our team
Our core purpose is to serve Irish shoppers a little better every day and being a
Customer Delivery Driver
you are the first face our customers see.
Being a Customer Delivery Driver is hands on, physical and full of variety. No two shifts are ever the same – customer’s look for help in all kinds of different ways.
For most of the day you’ll feel like your own boss, delivering to your customers but with a team of managers and colleagues back at base ready to support you when you need them.
Shift Pattern:
Various shifts available
You will be responsible for
Providing an excellent home shopping experience by putting our customers at the heart of everything we do is our main responsibility.
Loading the van where required, and check your van for roadworthines
Understanding the schedule and route that has been calculated for you
Looking the part in your uniform, ready to help our customers
Driving safely, responsibly and within the law
To be courteous to all road users
Serving your customer with a smile and greet them by name
Taking care of your customer’s deliveries as if they were your own
You will need
To have had a full IRISH or EU driving licence (manual or automatic) for at least 2 years with no more than 3 penalty points
To be a safe and courteous drivers
To enjoy helping others
To be personable with a good sense of humour and excellent communication skills
The ability to take the initiative and use common sense
To care about making a difference for customers and colleagues
The ability to stay calm under pressure
Please be aware that as part of our recruitment process, job offers are subject to the Garda Vetting Process and you will need to provide proof of current penalty points on your licence at Assessment Stage. This can be requested from the National Driver Licence Services (NDLS) on
1890 41 61 41. Press Option 4 and quote your driver number.
We are sorry but if you have been disqualified from driving within the last 10 years, we will not be able to accept your application.
Should you be successful in your application, your offer will be subject to and conditional upon you providing your bank account details before your agreed start date.
Whats in it for you?
We offer excellent benefits that help make Tesco a great place to work. These include but aren’t limited to:
A variety of shifts
Part time and full time contracts available between 20 -  39 hours   a week
An hourly rate of pay for new drivers of €18.24 per hour with additional premium for Sunday working
Annual Bonus Scheme
Colleague Clubcard offering 10% discount across stores and online, with 15% discount weekends once a month (Friday to Sunday), and 20% off twice a year. There is also 20% off F&F clothing, all year long, these various discounts can be extended to a family member with a 2
nd
Clubcard available.*
Our Virtual GP service provides free and confidential access to an online GP through video GP consultations, and online prescription service for colleagues. The service is also available to families of colleagues who live at the same address for a reduced cost.
24/7 access to our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) for you and family members for in the moment emotional support along with free access to a range of wellbeing services supporting you under our new Wellbeing First approach of Body, Mind and Life.
Life Assurance
Pension Plan*
Save As You Earn Scheme*
Paid Family Leave
Bike to Work
Long Service Awards
Commuter Scheme
*Entry requirements and rules of the scheme apply
About Us
Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer’s favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move.  Our core purpose is “Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day”.  Serving means more than a transactional relationship with our customers.  It means acting as a responsible and sustainable business for all stakeholders, for the communities we are part of, and for the planet. Through initiatives like the Tesco Community Fund, our association with Children’s Health Foundation, our partnership with FoodCloud and our Stronger Starts programme, we have supported over 21,000 community groups, raised over €7.5 million for medical equipment, and provided almost 15 million meals nationwide, to those living in food insecurity.
Tesco has operated in the Irish retail market since 1997, and with 190+ stores nationwide, we employ over 13,000 people in cities and towns around Ireland, supporting almost 45,000 jobs directly and indirectly. We partner with over 500 Irish suppliers - of which almost three-quarters are small and medium enterprises - which in turn supports almost 13,000 farming families around Ireland. Tesco is the single largest buyer of Irish food and drink in the world, buying €1.6 Billion a year; more than any other single country in the European Union, more than even the USA which you perceive as a massive buyer of Irish food.
We work closely with suppliers across Ireland who are dedicated to making the best products for our customers and this is reflected in the numerous awards our products have won over the years including Blás Na hÉireann, World Steak Challenge and Great Taste Awards.
We are proud to have an inclusive culture at Tesco where everyone truly feels able to be themselves. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated.   At Tesco, we not only celebrate diversity, but recognise the value and opportunity it brings.  We always want our colleagues to feel they can be themselves at work and we are committed to helping them be at their best.
We know life looks a little different for each of us. That’s why at Tesco, we always welcome chats about flexible working. Some people are at the start of their careers, some want the freedom to do the things they love. Others are going through life-changing moments like becoming a carer, nearing retirement, adapting to parenthood, or something else. So, talk to us throughout your application about how we can support.
Tesco is committed to celebrating diversity and everyone is welcome at Tesco. We're committed to providing a fully inclusive recruitment process, allowing candidates the opportunity to thrive and inform us of any reasonable adjustments they may require. For further information on the accessibility support we can offer, please click http://roi.tesco-careers.com/accessibility/
How can I let Tesco know I need additional support?
Please let us know you need additional support by emailing
tescoireland.recruitment@tesco.ie
This will allow us to understand more about you and how we can best support you through the recruitment process.

jobs.title: Kinisla Engineering Graduate 2027
jobs.desc:
Start Your Career with Kinisla!
Join the Kinisla Graduate Programme in a permanent, full-time role designed for ambitious graduates who aspire to become future senior leaders in our business. This is more than an entry-level graduate job: it is a structured two-year leadership development programme commencing September 2027. It combines formal learning, hands-on operational experience, meaningful projects, mentoring across the business. From day one, you will be challenged to build the commercial, operational and leadership capabilities needed to grow your career with Kinisla.
Assessment centres will take place during the week commencing 18 January 2027. As part of the selection process, you must be available to attend in person during that week.
Working in Engineering at Kinisla:
At Kinisla, Engineering is central to the safe, efficient and sustainable operation of our business. From milk intake through processing to final product packaging, our engineers help ensure every stage of our vertically integrated value chain performs at its best. As a graduate, you will join an experienced team and contribute to live engineering activities and projects from day one. You will work closely with Operations, Supply Chain, Food Safety & Quality, Health & Safety and other teams across the business, building practical knowledge of our production facilities, technologies, processes and products.
Your responsibilities may include:
Supporting plant operations and troubleshooting equipment issues to maintain safe and reliable production
Contributing to continuous improvement initiatives focused on energy efficiency, waste reduction and process optimisation
Collaborating with Supply Chain, Food Safety & Quality, Health & Safety and Operations to deliver cross-functional solutions
Supporting the implementation of new technologies and automation systems
Participating in capital projects, including equipment upgrades and facility enhancements
Applying lean manufacturing principles and data-led decision-making to improve performance
Building practical knowledge of dairy technologies and processes, including pasteurisation and cheese production
Developing a strong understanding of Kinisla's product portfolio and its application across retail and foodservice channels
Developing Kinisla's Future Leaders
Our Graduate Programme is designed to accelerate your development and prepare you for increasing responsibility and future leadership opportunities at Kinisla. You will benefit from:
A permanent role with structured development over two years
Off-the-job learning modules, mentoring and group projects
Hands-on responsibility and meaningful project work from day one
Opportunities to build a broad network across Kinisla
By the end of the programme, you will have built strong engineering expertise, a broad understanding of the business and the leadership foundations to progress towards more senior roles at Kinisla.
Do You Have What It Takes?
You are on track to achieve, or have recently completed, a degree with at least a 2:1 classification in Engineering or a related discipline
You can demonstrate an interest in building a career in Engineering within an FMCG and/or food manufacturing environment
You are curious, open to learning and actively seek feedback
You are a self-starter who takes ownership, prioritises effectively and adapts to changing priorities
You can influence, listen and build trust with internal and external stakeholders
You are ambitious, challenge the status quo and look for practical ways to improve the business
You are flexible to work across different sites and functions
You are eligible to work permanently in the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland
Discover Your Future with Kinisla:
Kinisla is a vertically integrated dairy, nutritional ingredients and consumer foods business, built on more than 50 years of expertise in milk processing, dairy and nutritional ingredient technology, and product innovation.
Working in close partnership with 2,600 family farms, we produce high-quality, low-carbon-intensity milk for dairy and nutritional ingredient solutions, alongside a strong portfolio of trusted, market-leading consumer products and brands.
With manufacturing operations across Ireland, Northern Ireland and the UK, and a global customer reach, Kinisla is a trusted and forward-looking supplier of high-quality dairy products, ingredients and nutritional solutions. Our four business areas are Agribusiness, Dairy Ingredients, Nutritional Ingredients, and Consumer Foods.
Our purpose is to reimagine dairy for better food and a future worth farming for. Through expertise, innovation and responsible growth, we are helping to shape a more regenerative and climate-conscious future for our dairy.
Rooted in the South-West of Ireland, Kinisla combines deep heritage, global expertise and innovation to create exciting products, partnerships and careers. Our values are Together, Braver, and Further.

jobs.title: Senior Staff Verification Engineer
jobs.desc:
We are current looking for a
Senior Staff Verification Engineer
to join our growing team in Cork, Ireland, that is involved in development of integrated circuits at the heart of modern power systems.
In this position, the successful candidate will work with an experienced team and be exposed to the entire product lifecycle. This is an important role full of possibility to architect and develop an end-to-end verification solution, spanning the product lifecycle from definition and requirements through IC design, hardware emulation and silicon support.
At Vishay our vision is one of a unified verification paradigm for full system verification. This includes simultaneous verification of HW, FW and SW components that make up a product offering. We are seeking a verification expert with the appetite to join us on this journey.
This is a senior role with the opportunity to create real impact within the organization and build a promising career.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
include the following. Other duties may be assigned.
Design and development of a unified verification architecture for Vishay power products.
Design and specification of testbench and verification IP
Construction of testbench environments to align with unified verification strategy.
Creation of full-system test-plans with an emphasis on test-case portability through the product lifecycle.
Responsibility for product verification planning, execution, status and coverage.
Maintenance of engineering documents in accordance with quality processes.
Structured tracking and implementation of design improvements.
Compliance with any requirements set out by product safety manager.
Usage of continuous integration tools for test-case integration and automation.
Support for test-engineering, product engineering and operations as well as participation in ATE data reviews, limit reviews and device yield analysis.
Experience
Successful candidates will have most of the following:
PhD, post-graduate or degree qualification in Electronic Engineering or similar.

Ensure all plant utilities and facilities operate safely, reliably, and efficiently to support site production requirements.
Manage and optimise site utility systems including boilers, chillers, air compressors, refrigeration systems, HVAC, and associated infrastructure.

Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on reliability, efficiency, sustainability, and operational excellence.
Maintain accurate maintenance documentation and SAP PM records.

Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Sustainability Engineering, Marine Engineering, or a related discipline.
Minimum 5-7 years' experience in maintenance, utilities, facilities, energy management, or a related engineering environment.
Strong technical knowledge of utility systems such as boilers, chillers, refrigeration systems, compressed air systems, and associated plant infrastructure.
Experience developing maintenance strategies, asset management plans, and capital replacement programmes.
Experience managing engineering projects from concept through implementation.
Strong troubleshooting and root cause analysis capabilities.
Knowledge of maintenance management systems, preferably SAP PM.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
Preferred Experience:
Experience within pharmaceutical, biotech, medical device, food, chemical, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments.
Exposure to energy management programmes and sustainability initiatives.
Experience working with outsourced maintenance and specialist service providers.
Certified Energy Manager (CEM) qualification or equivalent energy management certification.
Familiarity with ISO-based energy management systems.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Ability to develop technical solutions and present recommendations to stakeholders.
Project management and organisational skills.
Commercial awareness and ability to justify capital investments.
Collaborative approach with excellent stakeholder management skills.
Proactive mindset focused on continuous improvement and operational excellence.
Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities.

Inclusion and diversity are key to us. We are committed to creating an inclusive recruitment experience and welcome applications from all qualified candidates. If you require any reasonable accommodation or support during the application or interview process, please
contact us
, and we will be happy to assist.

nd

jobs.title: EU Brand Protection Manager
jobs.desc:
Logitech is the Sweet Spot for people who want their actions to have a positive global impact while having the flexibility to do it in their own way.
